title: Degree bound from Fourier granularity
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional cube over the field with two elements to that field. Regard $f$ as a real-valued function on this cube by mapping its value $1$ to $1$ and its value $0$ to $0$, and transfer this function to the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ using the coordinatewise correspondence between binary values and signs. If every Fourier coefficient of the resulting function is an integer multiple of $2^{-k}$, then the algebraic degree of $f$ is at most $k$.
